page: OVHcloud c3-64 is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.3 GHz, with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, alongside 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng. The memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput, with Passmark memory scores reaching the top 10% tier and uncached large-block read bandwidth measured at 227.99 GB/sec. Cryptographic and mathematical capabilities are supported by hardware-level AES, SHA_NI, and AVX instructions, yielding strong results in Passmark encryption and physics tests. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also rank in the top 25%, with Redis handling 77.38 million operations per second.

While multi-threaded decompression and small-model LLM inference perform in the top 25%, single-threaded gzip compression and medium-model LLM inference fall into the average tier. The 2.0 GB of memory per core represents a lower RAM-to-CPU ratio, which may limit memory-bound applications but maximizes compute density. This resource profile is optimized for compute-heavy workloads, multi-threaded data processing, Redis caching layers, and database operations that benefit from dedicated physical cores and local NVMe storage.
